rule: Working branch never tracks trunk, and the first PR push sets the branch's own upstream
description: Every create or switch of the working branch runs through `plugin/skills/create-working-branch/scripts/create-working-branch.sh`, and the ACTION row of that script's header is the source for the rule that a newly created working branch carries no upstream: a branch that is new is created with `git switch --no-track -c <branch> <base commit>`, because creating it from a remote-tracking base such as `origin/main` would otherwise make it track trunk, letting a plain `git push` or a force-with-lease retry against the tracked upstream target trunk. The source pin is ONE span carrying both the condition (the branch is new) and the obligation (`git switch --no-track -c <branch> <base commit>`); dropping `--no-track` or rewriting either half turns the suite red. Eleven consumers keep the rule closed at its other points. Two pins in the same script carry the code. The creation span carries the condition (the branch ref `refs/heads/$branch_name` does not resolve, so neither the already-on-branch nor the existing-branch path is taken) and the obligation (`git switch --quiet --no-track -c "$branch_name" "$base_commit"`, starting from the resolved base object id), together with the existing-branch path that runs `git switch --quiet --no-guess` and then the upstream rule, and the already-on-branch path that runs the upstream rule without a switch. The upstream-rule span carries the read of `branch.$branch_name.remote` and `branch.$branch_name.merge`, the mismatch condition (an upstream is set, and it is kept only when the merge ref is `refs/heads/$branch_name`, the remote is not `.`, and the remote passes the identifier gate, so a half-set upstream is never kept), and the unset obligation (both keys are removed with `unset_config_key`). Dropping `--no-track`, retargeting the start point, skipping the upstream rule on either existing-branch path, rewriting the keep condition, or dropping either unset turns the suite red. Every push of the working branch runs through `plugin/skills/push-branch/scripts/push-branch.sh`, and six pins in that script carry the push-side clauses. The mode-selection span carries the explicit mode taken when `--remote` is given, the read of `branch.<b>.remote` and `branch.<b>.merge` for the current branch, the condition that either is set, and the guard that stops with the exact blocker `upstream does not match the working branch` when either is empty, when the merge ref is not `refs/heads/$current_branch`, or when the upstream remote fails the identifier gate, before upstream mode is selected. The origin-mode span carries the condition (no upstream, `--no-upstream origin`, and `remote.origin.url` set), the obligation (push to `origin` in origin mode), the deferral with a warning when `remote.origin.url` is unset, and the block when no upstream and no remote is supplied. The push span carries the single push of the refspec `${head_sha}^{commit}:refs/heads/$current_branch`, with no `-u` in any mode: the source is the captured commit by object id in peel form, which no refname can shadow because no refname can contain `^`, and the destination is the branch's own name. The upstream-record span carries the explicit upstream record: after a successful push in any mode other than upstream (that is, explicit and origin modes), the script itself writes `branch.$current_branch.remote` as the push remote and `branch.$current_branch.merge` as `refs/heads/$current_branch`, because `-u` records nothing for an object-id source, so the explicit and origin first pushes set an upstream named after the branch itself. The retry span carries the force-with-lease retry of a non-fast-forward, taken in upstream mode only, against the same push remote and the same object-id refspec. The `run_git_push` span carries the single `git push --porcelain` that every push and retry runs. Rewriting the comparison target, the blocker, the mode conditions, the refspec source or destination, adding `-u` to the push, dropping or reconditioning the upstream record or retargeting either of its writes, or retargeting the retry, turns the suite red. Three consumers pin the callers that select the modes. `plugin/skills/open-plan-pr/scripts/open-plan-pr.sh`, which runs every push of the open-plan-pr skill, carries two: the `push_script` assignment that names `skills/push-branch/scripts/push-branch.sh` under the plugin root, and the push span that adds `--on-reject warn --no-upstream origin` to the argument array and runs `bash "$push_script" "${push_args[@]}"` as a child process, so a branch with no upstream makes its first push to `origin`; `plugin/skills/push-branch/SKILL.md` requirement 2 passes `--no-upstream block` in its script invocation, so a remediation push with no upstream blocks rather than choosing a remote. Changing any flag, retargeting the push script, or replacing either call with a direct push turns the suite red. The script's behavior, including that a mismatched upstream blocks before any push that every push and retry writes only the branch's own ref, that the commit written is the captured one even when the branch ref is rewritten or a ref named after the commit exists, and that a failed upstream write blocks after the push, is additionally asserted by `tools/test_push_branch.sh`. The create-working-branch script's behavior, including that a new branch has no upstream and sits at the base commit and that an existing branch keeps only an upstream named after itself, is additionally asserted by `tools/test_create_working_branch.sh`. What these pins honestly guarantee is exactly that these twelve word sequences exist in these four named files; they claim nothing about meaning. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) the create-working-branch script lines outside the pinned spans, including the header WHY paragraph, the base resolution, the `read_config_value`, `unset_config_key`, and `resolve_commit` helper bodies, and the final checks that HEAD is on the branch and that a new branch is at the base commit, are outside these pins and rest on `tools/test_create_working_branch.sh`, and `plugin/skills/create-working-branch/SKILL.md`, which routes every create or switch through the script, is not named by this fixture; (2) the script lines between the pinned spans, including the upstream-mode push remote resolution (`branch.<b>.pushRemote`, then `remote.pushDefault`, then the upstream remote), the refusal of the `.` remote, the classification of the push result, and the `write_config_value` helper body with its blocker, are outside these pins and rest on `tools/test_push_branch.sh`; (3) the open-plan-pr script's parse of a `warning:` line from push-branch.sh, and the open-plan-pr skill's rule to record it as a warning, are outside the pinned spans and rest on `tools/test_open_plan_pr.sh`; (4) a meaning inversion around the pinned bytes, such as surrounding prose that makes the unset or the script optional, or script code added between the spans that rewrites a captured value, is invisible; (5) the pins see only the four files they name, and no fixture in this directory can detect a NEW branch-creating or branch-pushing skill that never carries these clauses, which is an absence defect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract.

source.pattern: branch is new `git switch --no-track -c <branch> <base commit>` (created true),

consumers.pattern: resolve_commit "refs/heads/$branch_name" branch_created=false if [ "$already_on_branch" = true ]; then apply_upstream_rule elif [ -n "$resolved_commit" ]; then git switch --quiet --no-guess "$branch_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || blocker "could not switch to working_branch" apply_upstream_rule else git switch --quiet --no-track -c "$branch_name" "$base_commit" >/dev/null 2>&1 || blocker "could not create working_branch from base"

apply_upstream_rule() { local upstream_remote upstream_merge read_config_value "branch.$branch_name.remote" upstream_remote="$config_value" read_config_value "branch.$branch_name.merge" upstream_merge="$config_value" [ -n "$upstream_remote" ] || [ -n "$upstream_merge" ] || return 0 if [ "$upstream_merge" = "refs/heads/$branch_name" ] && [ "$upstream_remote" != '.' ] \ && hivemind_assert_identifier "$upstream_remote"; then return 0 fi unset_config_key "branch.$branch_name.remote" unset_config_key "branch.$branch_name.merge"

if [ "$remote_seen" = true ]; then push_mode='explicit' push_remote="$remote_name" else read_config_value "branch.$current_branch.remote" upstream_remote="$config_value" read_config_value "branch.$current_branch.merge" upstream_merge="$config_value" if [ -n "$upstream_remote" ] || [ -n "$upstream_merge" ]; then [ -n "$upstream_remote" ] && [ -n "$upstream_merge" ] || blocker "upstream does not match the working branch" [ "$upstream_merge" = "refs/heads/$current_branch" ] || blocker "upstream does not match the working branch" hivemind_assert_identifier "$upstream_remote" || blocker "upstream does not match the working branch" push_mode='upstream'

elif [ "$no_upstream" = 'origin' ]; then read_config_value "remote.origin.url" if [ -z "$config_value" ]; then printf 'branch: %s
commit: %s
warning: %s
' "$current_branch" "$head_sha" \ "no upstream and no origin remote; push deferred" exit 0 fi push_mode='origin' push_remote='origin' else blocker "no upstream and no remote supplied" fi

push_args+=(--on-reject warn --no-upstream origin) if [ "$expect_commit_seen" = true ]; then push_args+=(--expect-commit "$expect_commit") fi push_rc=0 push_output="$(bash "$push_script" "${push_args[@]}" 2>"$push_err_file")" || push_rc=$?
